lecture_summary: The lecture develops superposition, interference, reflection, standing waves, and resonance, then applies boundary conditions to harmonics on strings and in pipes. Its central workflow is to identify nodes and antinodes, sketch the mode, relate length to wavelength, determine wave speed, use f = v/λ, and verify which harmonics are allowed. Representative calculations use string tension and linear density, hanging masses, pipe lengths, and harmonic-frequency ratios.

videos.title: Mechanical Waves Physics Practice Problems - Basic Introduction
videos.reason: Best compact foundation: covers wave speed, wavelength, frequency, string tension and linear density, plus standing-wave harmonics, nodes, antinodes, and representative string calculations.

videos.title: Beat Frequency Physics Problems
videos.reason: Directly covers the lecture’s beat-pattern application of superposition for nearby frequencies, with problem-solving examples not duplicated by the first video.

videos.title: Standing Waves In Organ Pipes - Closed & Open Tubes - Physics Problems
videos.reason: Applies standing-wave boundary conditions to open and closed pipes and calculates fundamental frequencies, harmonics, overtones, wavelengths, and pipe lengths.

coverage_gaps: No playlist entry strongly and directly covers point-by-point superposition, general constructive/destructive/partial interference, or waves passing through one another; the beat video covers only the nearby-frequency case.
No strong match covers fixed-end versus free-end pulse reflection, including inversion and the π phase change, or reflected/transmitted splitting at a boundary between media.
The playlist descriptions do not explicitly cover standing-wave formation from equal counter-propagating waves or explain why only resonant frequencies form stable patterns.

The pipe candidate does not explicitly promise the displacement-versus-pressure node/antinode reversal, closed–closed pipes, or the distinction between resonant-mode order and harmonic number in a closed–open pipe.
